Title: Torn Meniscus - Why Your Knee Buckles Going Down Stairs

Description:
About 850,000 meniscus procedures happen in the US every year. If your knee buckles or gives way on stairs, plus catches or clicks when you walk, that's the cartilage cushion between your thighbone and shinbone starting to tear.

Watch to find out the two very different causes (sports twist vs. age-related wear), why ignoring it speeds up arthritis, and the RICE + quad-strengthening routine that protects your knee.

Your knee buckles or gives way going down stairs - are you brushing it off? 😳

A torn meniscus can come from a sports twist (common in soccer, basketball, football) or from cartilage simply wearing down with age - no injury needed. Left alone, it speeds up knee osteoarthritis.

Ice it for 15-20 min every few hours, skip deep squats and twisting, then build quad strength with straight-leg holds. See a doctor if your knee locks or you can't bear weight.
